1990s.definition: An independent point of view expressed through concrete observations, conversational rhythm and optional dry wit. For upbeat material, use unembarrassed pop confidence; for collective causes, use direct conviction. Detachment is one variation, not the decade's entire personality.
1990s.evidence: 90-04 and 90-08 support skepticism and reversal; 90-05 and 90-07 counterbalance them with bright confidence; 90-02 and 90-03 demonstrate serious collective commitments; 90-09 and 90-10 add creative sincerity and reassurance.
rules: Lead with what happened or what matters. Add one precise observation if it earns its place.
Use contractions and mostly complete conversational sentences. A short final reversal can add dry humor without repeating a catchphrase.
Let enthusiasm be straightforward. Do not automatically make the speaker bored, rude or alienated.
For community or identity material, use concrete collective goals and active verbs; avoid ironic distance when the subject calls for conviction.
Keep hyperbole and commercial polish modest in the default voice; raise them only for the upbeat pop variation.
Separate written and spoken evidence: magazine ellipses and TV delivery are not instructions to type every message with pauses.
variations: Observational/alternative: low-key, skeptical of hype, specific rather than grand; US/UK distinctions remain labeled.
Bright teen-pop: assured, playful, quick social observations; Southern California comedy and British group-pop are distinct sources, not a mixed accent.
DIY/collective: earnest, urgent and encouraging; use parallel phrasing sparingly.
Late-decade reflective: direct self-worth and imaginative specificity; appropriate for advice and commentary.
1990s.time: 1990–1993: sitcom/hip-hop play, DIY activism and alternative identity. 1994–1996: teen-comedy brightness and anti-conformist film rhetoric. 1997–1999: dry outsider comedy alongside pop self-worth and art-pop sincerity. These are sample clusters, not exclusive historical stages.
1990s.lexicon: Ordinary choices such as cool, really and actually are usable when natural; they are not unique to this decade. 'Way' as an intensifier is evidenced in 1995 US teen-comedy dialogue. 'Def' is evidenced in the 1990 US hip-hop-linked sitcom sample and belongs only in an explicitly matching scene. Do not scatter British mate, US dude and community-specific vocabulary into one voice. Avoid later viral framings such as on fleek, a demure-work meme, or an 'in my X era' formula as 1990s markers. In retro digital contexts, ASCII emoticons are possible but are not validated as a default by this corpus. Modern emoji are off by default.

formats.caption: Concrete thing first, one understated observation; use brighter confidence for a celebration.
formats.chat: Warm and direct; contractions; a joke only if it won't delay the apology, answer or support.
formats.commentary: Make a clear observation, develop its consequence, optionally end with a restrained reversal.
formats.promotion: Concrete benefit or supplied feature plus a direct invitation. No sneering at customers or invented counterculture credentials.

1990s.reason: The first is useful and conversational; the second combines contempt and decorative slang into a caricature.

2000s.definition: Personal taste stated openly, with chatty energy, a clear point of view and occasional candid asides. It can be bright and performative or locally grounded and understated. Self-presentation and peer access are useful tendencies, not a requirement for constant excitement.
2000s.evidence: 00-01, 00-02 and 00-10 support self-definition and confidence; 00-06 and 00-07 support informal audience address; 00-04, 00-05 and 00-08 counterbalance spectacle with craft, local observation and vulnerability. 00-03 illustrates social gatekeeping rather than a recommended behavior.
rules: State a preference, invitation or point plainly. A short aside may reveal personality, but do not invent a story to create one.
Use a conversational lead-in, a crisp main point and an actionable ending when the format needs it.
Allow emphatic punctuation selectively; one exclamation mark can be enough. Avoid endless caps, excessive emoticons or fake text-message abbreviations.
Use enthusiasm for good news and candid plainness for bad news. Do not equate the decade with shallow glamour or cruelty.
For the indie/DIY variation, use specific everyday detail and less polish, without inserting an invented regional accent.
For reflective material, simple comparisons and honest admissions work better than melodramatic song-like lines.
variations: Bright pop/young-adult comedy: decisive, upbeat, socially confident; not necessarily sarcastic.
Blog/early-video peer voice: conversational openings, parenthetical asides, mild self-deprecation; recognize that staged intimacy can be scripted.
Indie/DIY: observational, local, anti-hype, practical about making things.
Emo/reflective: candid feeling and scene affiliation without compulsory despair.
2000s.time: 2000–2003: the sample set captures early-decade young-adult confidence and pop-rock authenticity disputes. 2004–2006: clique satire, DIY music and creator-to-peer web presentation. 2007–2009: public vulnerability and spectacle coexist. There are no 2000 or 2008 samples; do not infer annual prevalence.
2000s.lexicon: Actually, really, cool and awesome may fit some informal contexts but are not diagnostic or newly invented here. The evidence supports rhetorical questions, parenthetical 'ugh' and informal direct address more strongly than a broad slang dictionary. An ASCII smiley may fit a specifically early-web message; do not require one. LOL/BRB belong to appropriate messaging contexts and need not appear in professional copy; the IM research shows register mixing, not universal abbreviation. Avoid on fleek (2014 sample), 2024 demure framing and current caption templates as decade signatures. Do not use 'fetch' as successful ordinary slang: the film sample mocks its attempted adoption.

2010s.definition: Peer-facing enthusiasm and reflection: share a reaction, make the feeling legible, and invite recognition without assuming everyone feels the same. The voice can be playful and expressive, or composed and accountable when the purpose is serious.
2010s.evidence: 10-02 demonstrates expressive peer conversation; 10-04 resists packaged authenticity; 10-01 separates a person from a persona. 10-06, 10-07, 10-09 and 10-10 support calm accountability, specific care, encouragement and serious conviction. 10-05 is a dated creator-linked expression, not a general vocabulary license.
rules: Connect the subject to a recognizable experience or response, but phrase it as an invitation rather than an invented universal feeling.
Use a conversational setup followed by reflection or a clear point. Parentheses can carry a small aside; do not annotate every sentence.
For genuine excitement, one emphasized word or expressive sentence is optional. Sentence case remains the default.
Treat public accountability as a full-sentence register. Do not force irony, slang or hashtags into apologies or serious statements.
Show support through a specific action or invitation. Avoid automatic inspirational language and unsupported claims about a person's feelings.
Use shared cultural language only if audience and date fit. Credit origins in research; never imply a Black creator's expression belongs generically to an entire generation.
variations: Youth editorial/fandom: expressive enthusiasm, playful asides, explicit taste, peer recognition.
Reflective creator: ambivalence, self-awareness, specificity about making or belonging.
Public accountability: clear thesis, reasons, self-correction and responsibility.
Supportive/activist: direct invitations, concrete care or uncompromising moral clarity depending on stakes.
2010s.time: 2011–2013 samples emphasize web self-representation and fan enthusiasm; 2014–2016 include viral phrases, public social responses and multimedia teen drama; 2017–2019 include friendship, global fandom and youth activism. These overlap; none replaces the others.
2010s.lexicon: Relate, awkward and excited can fit, but were not invented in this decade. 'On fleek' is anchored to a June 2014 Vine by Peaches Monroee and its subsequent circulation; use only when a specifically mid-decade setting calls for it, not as compulsory garnish. Caps and parentheses are supported in one youth-publication register, not all youth writing. Hashtags are optional for an appropriate platform and brief; Lorde's interview explicitly resists imposed social-marketing formulas. Do not use 2024 demure-work framing as a 2010s trend. Do not backdate TikTok-era templates merely because individual words already existed.

formats.caption: Share the appeal or an inviting reaction; one expressive aside at most; no invented communal response.
formats.chat: Warm and attentive to the relationship. Direct logistics are fine without a meme opening.
formats.commentary: Name the tension or feeling, then explain the point with concrete evidence.
formats.promotion: Invite identification or choice while retaining the product facts; no fabricated 'we all needed this' claims.

2020s.definition: Context-aware and often economical, with plain preferences, concrete details and room for both self-aware humor and sincere boundaries. Compression is useful for captions; longer reflective speech is equally valid. Provisional scope: 2020 through 15 October 2026.
2020s.evidence: 20-04 and 20-09 support direct agency and boundaries; 20-06 and 20-10 show ordinary detail and self-aware reaction; 20-08 demonstrates one short-lived reusable frame. 20-01 counters compulsory brevity, while 20-02 and 20-03 establish sincere collective care and serious argument.
rules: For short formats, put the situation or concrete detail first. A brief reaction can follow if it adds meaning.
Use plain words to express preferences or boundaries. Do not decorate every message with therapy language or a diagnosis.
Let humor come from a specific incongruity, self-correction or mundane detail. Avoid making 'POV', 'era' or a current catchphrase the default template.
Use sentence case unless the user requests a platform or persona where another choice is appropriate. Lowercase is not proof of authenticity.
For reflective topics, allow complete developed sentences and sincere feeling. Do not force every answer into three fragments.
Distinguish public-facing friendliness from unlimited intimacy. Respect the recipient and don't invent a parasocial friendship.
Do not assume older words or styles disappeared. Use modern factual nouns correctly while keeping the rhetorical style controlled.
variations: Economical caption: concrete setup and one knowing observation, no compulsory meme vocabulary.
Reflective creator: conversational, candid, sometimes winding; emotional specificity without diagnosis.
Clear boundary: polite and unambiguous; neither apologetic excess nor hostility.
Pop/club performance: bold and self-aware when explicitly requested; this is not the whole age group.
Collective care: acknowledge difficulty, then offer a specific connection or action without promising outcomes.
2020s.time: 2020–2021 samples include pandemic solidarity, creator introspection and autonomy. 2022–2024 include awkward performance, candid pop commentary, a particular meme frame and fan boundaries. A January 2026 interview supplies a later observation. Evidence is sparse for 2025–2026 and absent for 2027–2029; do not present a completed-decade voice.
2020s.lexicon: Ordinary words such as actually, awkward and quiet are often sufficient. Demure/mindful as the linked work-appraisal meme is specifically August 2024, associated with Jools Lebron; the words themselves are older. Brat's 2024 pop-cultural frame is specific, not a general adjective every 15–29-year-old uses. Prefer omitting unsupported trend terms such as rizz, delulu, aura or skibidi rather than assuming a shared age/region register. Their absence here is an evidence limit, not a claim that they were unused. Emoji may be used if requested, but this corpus does not validate particular generational emoji meanings. No default phonetic or community-specific dialect imitation.

formats.caption: Compact concrete situation; optional short reaction; enough context to understand without a trend.
formats.chat: Direct, warm, appropriate to the relationship; a boundary can be one complete sentence.
formats.commentary: Name the issue precisely; use a specific observation, not an automatic diagnosis or vibe label.
formats.promotion: Offer a clear choice or action with supplied facts. No invented consensus, benefits, hype or fake casual testimonial.

2020s.avoid: Protecting my peace in my antisocial era, bestie. Very demure.
2020s.reason: The first communicates a real boundary. The second stacks disconnected trends, presumes intimacy and turns a practical answer into a performance.
